quarterly_data.quarter: NVIDIA press release: NVIDIA and Semiconductor Leaders Advance AI Across Chip (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: At SEMICON West NVIDIA introduced cuPotential, a new CUDA-X library for simulating atomic and molecular interactions (available in early access; in early-access testing it accelerated already GPU-optimized workflows by an additional 2-3x), and named semiconductor companies adopting its CUDA-X libraries and AI stack for chip design, manufacturing and test ('AI-defined fabs'): Synopsys (early cuPotential adopter; uses cuPotential, cuEST and cuDSS - early QuantumATK results show a potential 30x speedup with cuEST, S-Device benchmarks a 12x speedup with cuDSS); Cadence (accelerated computing, Nemotron and CUDA-X; AuraStack AI Super Agent optimizing advanced packages 8x faster using cuDSS); Siemens (cuLitho to speed Calibre); Lam Research (intends to integrate NanoVDB into SEMulator3D, expected to accelerate select wafer-etch modeling by up to 30x; targeted for release by the end of this year); KLA (a new NPP NCC kernel 50x faster than earlier CPU versions); Teradyne (NPP, RAPIDS cuDF and CuPy for approximately 85x faster probe-maintenance inference); Advantest (Nemotron and Kumo-Anomaly integrated into ACS RTDI, powered by NVIDIA Grace Blackwell systems); Applied Materials (Omniverse and CUDA-X, up to 35x faster chamber simulations); also COMSOL (up to 10x faster simulations with cuDSS), Voltai, ChipAgents, Luminary, imec (30% improvement in the lithography process window), Analog Devices, FANUC, Foxconn and OMRON. Tim Costa (VP and GM, industrial and computational engineering): 'As fabs race to meet demand for advanced chips, NVIDIA CUDA-X and Omniverse libraries give AI agents accelerated simulation and inspection tools.'
quarterly_data.figure: cuPotential 2-3x; Synopsys potential 30x / 12x; Cadence 8x; Lam up to 30x; KLA 50x; Teradyne approximately 85x; Applied Materials up to 35x; COMSOL up to 10x; imec 30%
